body:
Reply with plain text only, no JSON, no preamble, and do not send messages to anyone else. Do not ask questions; decide.

You are writing short item texts for a Halloween D&D video game, "The Crooked Moon", set in and around Wickermoor, a timber-framed farming village in perpetual Halloween night under a crooked moon. Each item needs two texts:
- SUMMARY: one short plain sentence for the inventory, what the thing is, in plain modern English (no dialect). For a valuable, end with "Worth N gold." using the number given.
- TEXT: what you read or notice when you look closely. For a note, letter, card or page, TEXT is the words written on it, in the writer's own voice, under 60 words, signed only if the facts say so. For an object, TEXT is one or two sentences in second person, present tense, of a concrete detail (no game words, never tell the reader what to feel).

Rules: our own words. Use only the facts given; invent no new named people, places or history. No em dashes, no semicolons, no brackets. Village folk write plainly, with a country turn of phrase now and then, and spell correctly.

Output format, nothing else: for each item, a block exactly like

ITEM sock_of_coins
NAME: a short item name (two to five words)
SUMMARY: ...
TEXT: ...

ITEMS:

ITEM crooked_wicker_charm
Facts: a small charm of twisted wicker shaped like a crooked six-pointed star, found hidden in the barber's cellar. Worth nothing to a merchant. It smells of lamp smoke. Whoever made it twisted every strand the wrong way round.

ITEM offering_tin
Facts: a dented tin of old offering coins from under a flagstone in the abandoned church, the coins green with age. Worth 15 gold.

ITEM sock_of_coins
Facts: a wool sock heavy with coins, found up a cottage chimney, black with soot. Worth 12 gold.

ITEM roll_of_old_coins
Facts: a roll of old coins in waxed paper from behind a brick in the inn's cellar, minted with a face nobody in the village would know now. Worth 20 gold.

ITEM somerton_signet
Facts: a heavy gold signet ring stamped with an oak leaf, the mayor's family seal, hidden in the back of his desk. Worth 35 gold.

ITEM lost_purse
Facts: a little leather purse caught in the river reeds, wet, coins still in it, with initials stitched inside that no one has claimed. Worth 18 gold.

ITEM lockwood_spoons
Facts: a rusted tin of tarnished silver spoons, each handle engraved with a curly L, buried by the dead tree on the Druskenvald estate long before the Druskenvalds came. Worth 30 gold.

ITEM hearthstone_locket
Facts: a tarnished silver locket found under a hearthstone in the Crooked House parlour; the tiny portrait inside has been scratched out with a pin. Worth 40 gold.

ITEM hickock_playbill
Facts: a printed playbill left in a traveller's trunk upstairs at the Green Queen Inn: Hickock and Company present "The Prince in Gold", a travelling troupe soon to play the inn's little theatre. Text is the playbill's own printed words, showy and grand.

ITEM pupils_field_list
Facts: a pupil's list taken off them by the schoolteacher, in a child's round hand: the things their teacher sent them out to gather on a field trip: a button from Pip Oakum, a fact from Old Rusty, a thread of the bell-rope, a chalk mark from the church, with doodles of a goat in the margin. Unsigned.

ITEM holly_recipe_card
Facts: a floury recipe card for sick-bed broth in the baker Holly Aster's hand, kept in her flour bin. On the back she has admitted, to herself only, that the butcher Siv's bones make the better broth and she will never say so aloud. Signed H.

ITEM marianna_clover_note
Facts: a note the stablemistress Marianna Grey wrote to herself and pinned under the hay: when the clocktower bell tolls, her grey mare Clover bolts up the moor road, and she always ends up in the thicket by the north wall. Bring a halter and an apple, and talk low. Signed M.

ITEM lockwood_wage_page
Facts: an old page torn from a household account book, found in a feed bin in the barn of the house on the hill: wages for a butler, Mr. Patrini, and below it a smaller line for "the boy", with the last month's entry never filled in. Written in a clerk's neat hand, very old. Unsigned.
result:
ITEM crooked_wicker_charm
NAME: Crooked Wicker Charm
SUMMARY: A small charm of twisted wicker shaped like a crooked six-pointed star.
TEXT: You turn the brittle star in your fingers and catch the dry scent of lamp smoke clinging to the reed. Every single strand of wicker is twisted the wrong way round.

ITEM offering_tin
NAME: Old Offering Tin
SUMMARY: A dented tin of old offering coins from the abandoned church. Worth 15 gold.
TEXT: You pry back the dented lid to find a heap of old church coins packed tight inside. Every piece is crusted green with age from lying under the cold flagstone.

ITEM sock_of_coins
NAME: Sooty Sock of Coins
SUMMARY: A soot-blackened wool sock heavy with coins from a cottage chimney. Worth 12 gold.
TEXT: Coarse black soot rubs off onto your palm as you heft the heavy woollen toe. Loose coins clink softly together inside the thick knit.

ITEM roll_of_old_coins
NAME: Roll of Old Coins
SUMMARY: A waxed paper roll of old coins found behind a cellar brick at the inn. Worth 20 gold.
TEXT: You peel back a corner of the stiff waxed paper and brush cellar mortar from the top coin. The worn metal bears the profile of a ruler no one in the village could name today.

ITEM somerton_signet
NAME: Gold Oak-Leaf Signet
SUMMARY: A heavy gold signet ring bearing the mayor's family seal. Worth 35 gold.
TEXT: You tilt the heavy gold band to the light and trace the deep stamp of an oak leaf across its face. The inner rim is worn smooth from years of quiet use.

ITEM lost_purse
NAME: River-Soaked Leather Purse
SUMMARY: A wet leather purse with coins inside, pulled from the river reeds. Worth 18 gold.
TEXT: River water still darkens the soft leather as you pull open the damp drawstring to check the coins within. Faded thread inside the lip forms a pair of stitched initials that no one has claimed.

ITEM lockwood_spoons
NAME: Tin of Silver Spoons
SUMMARY: A rusted tin of tarnished silver spoons buried on the Druskenvald estate. Worth 30 gold.
TEXT: Dark tarnish dulls the bowls of the spoons resting inside their flaking tin box. You rub your thumb across a handle to reveal a curly letter L cut deep into the silver.

ITEM hearthstone_locket
NAME: Scratched Silver Locket
SUMMARY: A tarnished silver locket found beneath a hearthstone in the Crooked House parlour. Worth 40 gold.
TEXT: Ash from under the hearthstone clings to the clasp as you thumb the tarnished silver case open. Inside, someone has taken a sharp pin and scratched the tiny painted face down to bare metal.

ITEM hickock_playbill
NAME: Green Queen Playbill
SUMMARY: A printed playbill for a travelling theatre troupe performing at the Green Queen Inn.
TEXT: Hear ye, gentle patrons of the Green Queen Inn! Hickock and Company proudly present that most dazzling tragedy, The Prince in Gold, coming soon to grace this very stage for your wonder and delight!

ITEM pupils_field_list
NAME: Pupil's Field-Trip List
SUMMARY: A handwritten list of field-trip tasks taken from a pupil by the schoolteacher.
TEXT: Things to get for teacher. One button off Pip Oakum. One true fact out of Old Rusty. A bit of thread from the bell-rope. A rub of chalk off the church wall.

ITEM holly_recipe_card
NAME: Floury Broth Recipe Card
SUMMARY: A flour-dusted recipe card for sick-bed broth written by the baker Holly Aster.
TEXT: Simmer the root and barley slow and skim the top clean before you salt it. The truth is Siv's marrow bones make a far better broth than mine ever does, though I would bite my tongue clean through before I said a word of it to him. H.

ITEM marianna_clover_note
NAME: Note About Clover
SUMMARY: A reminder note written by the stablemistress Marianna Grey about her grey mare Clover.
TEXT: When that clocktower bell starts up, Clover will bolt straight up the moor road like the hounds are on her tail. Look for her tangled up in the thicket by the north wall. Take a halter and a sweet apple, and mind you talk low to her. M.

ITEM lockwood_wage_page
NAME: Torn Household Wage Page
SUMMARY: An old torn page of servant wages from a household account book.
TEXT: Household wages paid in full. To Mr. Patrini, butler, for his keeping of the hall and cellar, four crowns the month. To the boy, for carrying wood and tending the grates, sixpence. For the month following, paid to Mr. Patrini, and to the boy, nothing entered.
